audit_findings.title: Historical OE may mix consolidated and common-equity claims
audit_findings.mechanism: Inconsistent attribution of net income, D&A, working capital and maintenance capital spending would distort the 2018–2021 OE observations and therefore the log-trend anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company's Consolidated Financial Statements include all subsidiaries in which the Company has the ability to exercise direct or indirect control over operating and financial policies.
audit_findings.explanation: The consolidation policy is demonstrated, but the supplied record does not show which attributable or consolidated figures entered the OE calculation or quantify the historical NCI gaps. The latest balance sheets show only $1 million of NCI, but that does not resolve 2018–2021. A claim mismatch remains possible, while its direction and ability to change the $623 million anchor cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild 2018–2021 using a consistent GPK-common-equity perimeter for every OE component, then rerun the log trend; alternatively rerun the anchor excluding those years and compare all scenario values and buy-below prices.

audit_findings.title: Required environmental capital spending may be absent from forecast OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $65 million in 2026 and $147 million in 2027; $212 million total; computed gross PV at 10% of $180.6 million, or $0.60 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: Required compliance capital spending reduces forecast OE dollar-for-dollar if it is not already included in the maintenance-capex allowance.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2026 and 2027, the Company estimates it will spend $65 million and $147 million respectively, primarily for projects such as upgrades to and new wastewater treatment systems at certain of its paperboard manufacturing facilities.
audit_findings.explanation: Omission is not demonstrated because the maintenance-capex allowance is not itemized. Even treating the entire filed $212 million as incremental, with no tax or overlap adjustment, reduces value by only about $0.60 per share. Base value would remain approximately $28.96 per share and its 30% MOS threshold approximately $20.27, still far above the $10.43 market price. This conservative scale comparison does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Map the $65 million and $147 million project budgets to forecast maintenance capex, remove any overlap with the normalized allowance, and rerun only the net incremental amounts.

audit_findings.title: The maintenance-versus-growth capex split rests on deficient controls
audit_findings.magnitude: $922 million of 2025 capital spending, including $737 million described as adding capacity and improving process capabilities; computed recurring anchor reduction of about $316 million would lower the base MOS threshold to the $10.43 market price
audit_findings.mechanism: Misclassifying unavoidable recurring investment as growth capex overstates OE and the anchor; classifying discretionary growth investment as maintenance capex understates them.
audit_findings.evidence: Specifically, there is a lack of transparency related to certain capital expenditures, which resulted in the Company exceeding the delegation of authority for certain capital projects as well as the annual Board-approved capital expenditure limits.
audit_findings.explanation: The control failure and unauthorized capital expenditures are demonstrated, although the filing says they caused no financial-statement misstatement. The valuation error itself remains unresolved because project economics and the OE capex classifications are not supplied. The exposed pool is nevertheless large enough to matter: approximately $316 million of recurring anchor overstatement would consume the base-case purchase-price cushion, versus $737 million classified as capacity and process spending in 2025. A sufficiently large classification error is therefore reasonably capable of changing the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every material 2025 and 2026 project—including unauthorized overruns, Waco completion costs, capital spares, mill reliability work and the cancelled $40 million warehouse project—to maintenance or growth criteria; then rebuild historical OE and rerun the anchor and scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized interest may escape the equity-level OE charge
audit_findings.magnitude: $52 million in 2025 and $34 million in 2024; computed conservative perpetual-$52-million base-value effect of $730.6 million, or $2.41 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Capitalized interest avoids current interest expense and would also avoid OE if the associated capital spending were excluded as growth, contrary to the equity-level treatment of financing costs.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company capitalized interest of $52 million and $34 million in 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: Capitalization is demonstrated, but omission from OE is not. As a conservative upper-bound test, permanently reducing the $623 million anchor by the full 2025 amount would lower base value from $29.56 to about $27.15 per share and the base MOS threshold to about $19.00, still well above $10.43. The actual effect should be smaller because the charge was project-related, the trend anchor dilutes a one-year correction, and only $3 million was capitalized in the first half of 2026.
audit_findings.action: Trace capitalized interest through deducted and excluded capital-spending categories for every historical year; correct any double escape and rerun the log-trend anchor.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 interest expense may not represent the post-refinancing burden
audit_findings.magnitude: $400 million refinanced at 5.47% versus 1.512%; computed annual pre-tax increase of $15.8 million; conservative perpetual base-value effect of about $222.4 million, or $0.73 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Higher post-refinancing interest reduces equity-level OE because debt is not deducted in the bridge and interest expense is intended to remain in OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The new term loan will bear interest at a floating rate per annum, ranging from SOFR plus 1.00 % to SOFR plus 1.75 %, or base rate plus 0.00 % to base rate plus 0.75 %, determined using a pricing grid based on GPIL's consolidated total leverage ratio from time to time, and GPIL's election of SOFR or base rate as the reference rate.
audit_findings.explanation: The mismatch is demonstrated: the $400 million note was replaced in April 2026, and the new loan carried 5.47% at June 30. The computed rate difference implies approximately $15.8 million of additional annual interest before tax. Even treating that temporary increase as permanent would reduce the base value to about $28.83 per share and the base MOS threshold to about $20.18, still far above $10.43. The actual loan matures in June 2027, so the likely effect is smaller.
audit_findings.action: Normalize the forecast using actual 2026 interest expense, the loan's effective rate, hedges and its June 2027 maturity; ensure the adjustment is coordinated with capitalized-interest treatment to avoid double counting.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded benefit obligations may be an unbridged senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $88 million accrued pension and postretirement benefits at June 30, 2026; expected 2026 contributions of $10–$15 million plus approximately $1 million for postretirement healthcare; $88 million equals $0.29 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: A net funded-status deficit could reduce the equity bridge, while cash contributions exceeding pension expense would reduce forecast OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company expects to make contributions in the range of $ 10 million to $ 15 million in 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filed liability is only about 1% of the $8.958 billion base equity value. Even deducting the entire $88 million from the bridge would reduce base value from $29.56 to about $29.27 per share and the base MOS threshold to about $20.49, still far above $10.43. Expected annual contributions are also only 1.8%–2.6% of the $623 million anchor. Treatment should be verified, but the filed amounts cannot change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the June 2026 funded status, current and noncurrent liabilities, pension assets, accounting expense and cash contributions; include contributions in OE or deduct the net deficit in the bridge, but not both.
